# SPEC — NODE PHYSICAL TOPOLOGY
Owner directive (Bane, 2026-11-21, quoted verbatim): "one bunker instance for a project where there's, I mean, one physical system per bunker. Technically multiple bunkers in the unit, physical system."

## The mapping
1. **One bunker instance serves exactly one project** — one bunker agent, one repo, one harness (unchanged from this spec's definition of a node). 2. **One bunker runs on one physical system.** A bunker never spans machines and two bunkers never share one `$HOME` or one harness port. 3. **Multiple bunkers MAY share one physical system (the unit).** Each co-tenant bunker must independently pass its own layer 00 footprint admission against the shared disk floor; one bunker's checkout, toolchains, harness home and node state are charged to that admission, never amortized across tenants. 4. **A bunker is CPU-only.** No GPU is provisioned on a node. Inference is served to nodes over the orchestration network by central inference racks; the node's harness points at the rack's OpenAI-compatible endpoint (the layer 20 `inference_key` row already carries this credential path).

## Resident-context requirement (the load-bearing constraint)
A lane re-primes nearly the same context every tick. Measured over the scheduler ticks ledger, 2026-10-22 → 2026-11-21 (30 days, 15,500 ticks): the average lane tick sends **4.15M in+cache tokens and produces 9.3K output tokens**, and the average worker session sends **5.9M in+cache tokens and produces 22K output tokens**. Projected over all 77 project families at standard lane cadences with worker waves (~2 per tick), the unconstrained fleet generates **~17B in+cache tokens/day and ~56M output tokens/day** — naive prefill demand of ~197K tok/s average, which no rationally-sized GPU fleet serves statelessly.
The design that makes this tractable is **resident KV / prefix cache per lane**: because a bunker runs one project forever, its lane context (board + repo + spec + AGENTS.md, the 4-6M-token body re-sent each tick) can stay resident in the serving rack and each tick's re-prime becomes a delta prefill (~5-10% of the body). With resident caches the same fleet's real prefill demand drops to ~1-2B tokens/day. Serving stacks that evict KV between ticks (stateless per-call serving) are non-conformant with this plan regardless of their decode speed.
The sizing census, projection math and rack plan live in `docs/HARDWARE-PLAN.md`.
